{"parentUuid":"ded0d472-79b7-4143-8e3d-7fc193b174d2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2cdac32f-54cc-46d2-94c0-21730bc710d0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01T9vX4gsdyhjpvg9iXTjBLZ","type":"tool_result","content":"commit f9475b715eadc966a93dd79c0f52575612142f83\nAuthor: maxillamas06-arch <maxillamas06@gmail.com>\nDate:   Sat Oct 10 16:08:31 2026 -0400\n\n    T01: Leader and members log in; members are refused leader screens\n    \n    - Accounts: argon2-hashed users in SQLite, login by email, one message for\n      a wrong password or unknown email, inactive users refused at login and\n      on every request (accounts.active_user).\n    - Sessions in a signed, HTTP-only, same-site cookie; one app-wide CSRF\n      check on every POST (403 with a Spanish page), including login and logout.\n    - Policy: LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES is the single declaration of leader-only\n      routes; the admin gate redirects anonymous requests to /login and answers\n      members with the Spanish \"No tienes permiso\" page, which keeps the menu.\n    - Spanish admin layout with a persistent menu, dashboard greeting by\n      nickname, and the read-only list of accounts (Cuentas).\n    - Seed rebuilds the database with the leader and two fictional members;\n      settings read .env (or .env.example on a fresh clone) so it runs with no\n      manual steps. Each test gets its own fresh temporary database.\n    - test_t00's admin check now signs in first: T01 puts /admin behind login.\n    \n    Code review findings and resolutions are on #2.\n    \n    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n    \n    Closes #2\n\n .env.example                       |   9 ++-\n README.md                          |  13 +++-\n app/accounts.py                    |  79 +++++++++++++++++++++\n app/cli.py                         |   3 +-\n app/db.py                          |  33 +++++++++\n app/main.py                        |  57 +++++++++------\n app/policy.py                      |  18 +++++\n app/routes/__init__.py             |   1 +\n app/routes/auth.py                 |  35 ++++++++++\n app/routes/dashboard.py            |  14 ++++\n app/routes/users.py                |  18 +++++\n app/settings.py                    |  28 +++++++-\n app/web.py                         |  78 +++++++++++++++++++++\n scripts/seed_demo.py               |  44 ++++++++----\n templates/admin/base.html          |  45 ++++++++++++\n templates/admin/csrf_rejected.html |   7 ++\n templates/admin/dashboard.html     |   6 ++\n templates/admin/forbidden.html     |   7 ++\n templates/admin/hello.html         |   5 --\n templates/admin/login.html         |  14 ++++\n templates/admin/users.html         |  22 ++++++\n tests/conftest.py                  | 139 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++------\n tests/test_t00.py                  |   8 ++-\n     250 docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_opus-high_20261010.md\n7:Club de Aficionados Albiazul is an unofficial fan club of Rayados (C.F. Monterrey). Its fans share opinions about the team (how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing), but today they post them on X and Facebook, where they are mixed in with everything else and impossible to find again. The fan club wants one place where fan opinions live, organized and easy to read.\n14:- **Member** (role *editor*): a fan with an account, created by the leader. Writes posts and submits them to the leader; cannot publish, cannot touch pages or accounts.\n22:- A **public site**: static HTML regenerated from published content only and deployed to GitHub Pages. A home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, a page per post, and the fan club's pages in the menu. Navy-and-white, playful, unmistakably Monterrey, never official.\n24:Every change readers can see passes through the leader (ADR-003): posts move draft → submitted → published, a member's change to a published post waits as a pending edit, and a member's nickname is chosen once.\n29:2. **Two roles.** *Admin* = the leader: everything. *Editor* = a member: writes, edits and submits their own posts, reads everyone's posts, proposes edits to their own published posts. Editors cannot publish, cannot see or change pages, cannot manage accounts, and cannot run a site update. Enforced on the server for every route, never by hiding links.\n30:3. **Posts.** A post is a fan's opinion: title, slug, Markdown body, exactly one topic, status (draft, submitted, published), author, and created/updated/published timestamps. Full create, read, update, delete, following the lifecycle below.\n31:4. **Pages.** Fixed fan-club information: same fields as a post minus the topic, plus a menu-order number. Only the leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes them. Published pages appear in the public menu in menu order.\n32:5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a content list filterable by status, topic and (leader only) post vs page, and an editor with a *Vista previa* that shows the sanitized result.\n34:7. **Public site and site update.** `cms publish` regenerates the public site from published posts and pages only, with sanitized Markdown, a menu built from published pages, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button does both.\n41:2. As the leader, I want a dashboard showing how many posts are waiting for review, so that I know at a glance whether I have checking to do.\n42:3. As the leader, I want the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts, pending edits, pages and active members, so that I can see the state of the site without opening lists.\n44:5. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to submitted posts, so that my review queue is one click away.\n45:6. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to posts with a pending edit, so that I can review changes to published posts.\n46:7. As the leader, I want to filter the content list by topic and by post vs page, so that I can find things quickly.\n47:8. As the leader, I want to read a submitted post exactly as readers would see it, so that I can judge whether it crosses from tiradera into a personal attack.\n48:9. As the leader, I want to publish a submitted post, so that it goes public at the next site update.\n49:10. As the leader, I want to send back a submitted post to draft, so that its member can rework it.\n53:14. As the leader, I want to unpublish a published post, so that it disappears from the public site at the next site update.\n54:15. As the leader, I want to be stopped from unpublishing a post while a pending edit waits, so that a member's proposed change is never silently thrown away.\n55:16. As the leader, I want to edit any post directly, so that I can fix a typo without a round trip; my edits to published posts go live at the next site update.\n56:17. As the leader, I want to write my own posts and publish them directly, so that fan club news does not wait on a review of myself.\n57:18. As the leader, I want to delete any post after confirming, so that content that should never have existed is gone.\n60:21. As the leader, I want to be prevented from giving a page a name the site already uses (such as the home page or a topic page), so that nothing on the site is overwritten.\n66:27. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's posts to stay up under their nickname, so that the fan club's archive is not broken.\n67:28. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's submitted posts and pending edits to stay in my queue, so that I still decide what happens to them.\n80:38. As a member, I want to write a post with a title, a topic and a Markdown body, so that I can share my opinion.\n81:39. As a member, I want the slug to be made from my title, keeping accents and ñ, so that the link reads like my title.\n82:40. As a member, I want to edit the slug until my post is first published, so that I can tidy the link.\n83:41. As a member, I want to press *Vista previa* and see exactly what readers will see, so that my formatting is right before I submit.\n86:44. As a member, I want to withdraw a submitted post back to draft, so that I can fix something before the leader reads it.\n88:46. As a member, I want to propose an edit to my own published post, so that I can correct it while the published version stays up.\n90:48. As a member, I want to see every post in the content list, including other members', so that I know what has already been written about Saturday's match.\n91:49. As a member, I want to be refused when I try to change someone else's post or reach a leader screen, so that the rules are real.\n96:51. As a reader, I want a home page with one section per topic showing its three newest posts, so that I can see what fans are saying about each subject.\n97:52. As a reader, I want a *Ver todos* link on each section, so that I can read every post in a topic.\n98:53. As a reader, I want each post to show its title, the author's nickname, its topic, and *Publicado el …* (and *Actualizado el …* if it changed after publishing), so that I know who said what and when.\n103:58. As a reader, I want links to keep working after I share them on X or Facebook, so that my friends land on the same post.\n105:60. As a reader, I never want to see drafts, submitted posts, pending edits, or anything the leader has not approved.\n115:- **Content.** Posts, pages and pending edits: storage, slug generation, and the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\n116:- **Markdown rendering.** One function: Markdown text in, sanitized HTML out (markdown-it-py, then nh3 with an allowlist). Used by *Vista previa*, the leader's review screens and the site export, so the preview is always exactly what readers get.\n117:- **Site export.** Renders every published post and published page, the topic pages and the home page into an output directory with relative, percent-encoded links. Called by `cms publish` and by the site update.\n119:- **Admin web layer.** Routes and Spanish templates for login, first-login nickname, *Mi cuenta*, dashboard, content list, post editor, page editor, review screens, users, site update, and the refusal page.\n120:- **Public templates.** Home, topic page, post page, page, shared layout with menu, topic links and disclaimer.\n126:- **Post**: id, title, slug (unique among posts), Markdown body, topic, status (*draft*, *submitted*, *published*), author (a user), created and updated timestamps, first-published timestamp (set once, never cleared; its presence locks the slug), and an edited-after-publishing timestamp (drives *Actualizado el …*).\n127:- **Pending edit**: at most one per post; proposed title, topic and Markdown body, created and updated timestamps. The slug is never part of a pending edit.\n128:- **Page**: id, title, slug (unique among pages, and never a reserved name), Markdown body, status (*draft* or *published*), menu-order number, author, created, updated and first-published timestamps.\n130:- **Topics** are a fixed list in code, not a table: Match (*Partido*), Lineup (*Alineación*), Coach (*Técnico*), Signings (*Fichajes*), Fan club news (*Noticias del club de aficionados*).\n132:### Post lifecycle\n143:| Approve | leader | pending edit | the edit replaces title, topic and body; pending edit removed; edited-after-publishing set |\n146:| Delete | the member who wrote it, drafts only; the leader, any post | any | post and its pending edit removed |\n148:The leader's own posts may be published straight from draft. A member never changes a submitted or published post directly. A member may read every post in the admin console but act only on their own.\n154:- Login identifier is the email. The test helper in `tests/conftest.py` already posts `email` and `password` to `/login`; its demo users are updated to match the seed's emails.\n157:- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token in a hidden field, including login, logout, *Vista previa* and the site update. A POST without a valid token gets 403.\n158:- Anonymous requests to any admin route redirect to `/login`. An editor requesting a leader-only route, or acting on someone else's post, gets 403 with a Spanish refusal page that keeps the admin menu. Unknown ids get 404.\n168:- `/login` (GET, POST), `/logout` (POST)\n170:- `/admin/content` content list with `status`, `topic`, `pending` and (leader only) `type` filters\n171:- `/admin/posts/new`, `/admin/posts/{id}` and one POST route per lifecycle action, plus a preview POST\n172:- `/admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit` side-by-side review (leader)\n173:- `/admin/pages/...` create, edit, publish, unpublish, delete, preview (leader only)\n175:- `/admin/site-update` (POST, leader only)\n179:### Slugs\n181:Made from the title: Unicode-normalized (NFC), lowercased, letters (including á é í ó ú ü ñ) and digits kept, every other run of characters replaced by a single hyphen, trimmed, capped at 80 characters. Example: *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`. A taken slug gets `-2`, `-3`, … A manually entered slug follows the same rules. A post's slug is editable until it is first published, then locked forever, so shared links keep working. Page slugs may not be a reserved name: `index`, `tema`, `posts`, `style`.\n183:### Markdown\n185:Rendered with markdown-it-py, then sanitized with nh3 using an allowlist of text-formatting tags, lists, blockquotes, code and links. Scripts, event-handler attributes and `javascript:` links are removed. **Images are removed too**: photo uploads are out of scope and the site must carry no official photos. Links get `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`.\n189:- `index.html`: one section per topic in the fixed order, each with its three newest published posts (title, nickname, date) and a *Ver todos* link; a topic with no published posts is hidden on the home page. A Cerro de la Silla banner on top.\n190:- `tema/<topic-slug>.html`: all published posts in that topic, newest first. All five topic pages are always generated (an empty one says so), so no link ever breaks.\n191:- `posts/<slug>.html`: title, nickname, topic link, *Publicado el …*, *Actualizado el …* when edited after publishing, and the body.\n192:- `<page-slug>.html`: a published page.\n194:- Every page shares a menu (*Inicio* plus published pages by menu order), a row of topic links, and the footer with a stadium silhouette above the disclaimer: *\"Sitio de aficionados. Sin afiliación con el Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* with *\"Fan site, not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* beneath.\n195:- Every `href` and `src` is relative (`../style.css` from nested pages) and percent-encoded, so accented slugs never break a link. Monterrey). Its fans share opinions about the team (how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing), but today they post them on X and Facebook, where they are mixed in with everything else and impossible to find again. The fan club wants one place where fan opinions live, organized and easy to read.\n14:- **Member** (role *editor*): a fan with an account, created by the leader. Writes posts and submits them to the leader; cannot publish, cannot touch pages or accounts.\n22:- A **public site**: static HTML regenerated from published content only and deployed to GitHub Pages. A home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, a page per post, and the fan club's pages in the menu. Navy-and-white, playful, unmistakably Monterrey, never official.\n24:Every change readers can see passes through the leader (ADR-003): posts move draft → submitted → published, a member's change to a published post waits as a pending edit, and a member's nickname is chosen once.\n29:2. **Two roles.** *Admin* = the leader: everything. *Editor* = a member: writes, edits and submits their own posts, reads everyone's posts, proposes edits to their own published posts. Editors cannot publish, cannot see or change pages, cannot manage accounts, and cannot run a site update. Enforced on the server for every route, never by hiding links.\n30:3. **Posts.** A post is a fan's opinion: title, slug, Markdown body, exactly one topic, status (draft, submitted, published), author, and created/updated/published timestamps. Full create, read, update, delete, following the lifecycle below.\n31:4. **Pages.** Fixed fan-club information: same fields as a post minus the topic, plus a menu-order number. Only the leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes them. Published pages appear in the public menu in menu order.\n32:5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a content list filterable by status, topic and (leader only) post vs page, and an editor with a *Vista previa* that shows the sanitized result.\n34:7. **Public site and site update.** `cms publish` regenerates the public site from published posts and pages only, with sanitized Markdown, a menu built from published pages, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button does both.\n41:2. As the leader, I want a dashboard showing how many posts are waiting for review, so that I know at a glance whether I have checking to do.\n42:3. As the leader, I want the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts, pending edits, pages and active members, so that I can see the state of the site without opening lists.\n44:5. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to submitted posts, so that my review queue is one click away.\n45:6. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to posts with a pending edit, so that I can review changes to published posts.\n46:7. As the leader, I want to filter the content list by topic and by post vs page, so that I can find things quickly.\n47:8. As the leader, I want to read a submitted post exactly as readers would see it, so that I can judge whether it crosses from tiradera into a personal attack.\n48:9. As the leader, I want to publish a submitted post, so that it goes public at the next site update.\n49:10. As the leader, I want to send back a submitted post to draft, so that its member can rework it.\n53:14. As the leader, I want to unpublish a published post, so that it disappears from the public site at the next site update.\n54:15. As the leader, I want to be stopped from unpublishing a post while a pending edit waits, so that a member's proposed change is never silently thrown away.\n55:16. As the leader, I want to edit any post directly, so that I can fix a typo without a round trip; my edits to published posts go live at the next site update.\n56:17. As the leader, I want to write my own posts and publish them directly, so that fan club news does not wait on a review of myself.\n57:18. As the leader, I want to delete any post after confirming, so that content that should never have existed is gone.\n60:21. As the leader, I want to be prevented from giving a page a name the site already uses (such as the home page or a topic page), so that nothing on the site is overwritten.\n66:27. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's posts to stay up under their nickname, so that the fan club's archive is not broken.\n67:28. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's submitted posts and pending edits to stay in my queue, so that I still decide what happens to them.\n80:38. As a member, I want to write a post with a title, a topic and a Markdown body, so that I can share my opinion.\n81:39. As a member, I want the slug to be made from my title, keeping accents and ñ, so that the link reads like my title.\n82:40. As a member, I want to edit the slug until my post is first published, so that I can tidy the link.\n83:41. As a member, I want to press *Vista previa* and see exactly what readers will see, so that my formatting is right before I submit.\n86:44. As a member, I want to withdraw a submitted post back to draft, so that I can fix something before the leader reads it.\n88:46. As a member, I want to propose an edit to my own published post, so that I can correct it while the published version stays up.\n90:48. As a member, I want to see every post in the content list, including other members', so that I know what has already been written about Saturday's match.\n91:49. As a member, I want to be refused when I try to change someone else's post or reach a leader screen, so that the rules are real.\n96:51. As a reader, I want a home page with one section per topic showing its three newest posts, so that I can see what fans are saying about each subject.\n97:52. As a reader, I want a *Ver todos* link on each section, so that I can read every post in a topic.\n98:53. As a reader, I want each post to show its title, the author's nickname, its topic, and *Publicado el …* (and *Actualizado el …* if it changed after publishing), so that I know who said what and when.\n103:58. {"parentUuid":"d7f284c6-2151-4f02-bef6-681a87606816","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2cdac32f-54cc-46d2-94c0-21730bc710d0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"088e5699-352a-4e5f-9119-b597c047f4a5","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:16:17.518Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01MgiLcPXBpiDWCWyNvdr3ab","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9bedde74-7160-4dff-9700-957083ce192b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"3ea8183b-75c4-440d-8ce3-ff89fc858bc2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2cdac32f-54cc-46d2-94c0-21730bc710d0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GBfKZC6r5kNWDz6MCfd9EP","type":"tool_result","content":"### T03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe leader publishes a post and, after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, readers see it on GitHub Pages: a home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, and a page per post with the author's nickname and a Spanish date, all inside the striped navy-and-white layout with the disclaimer. Drafts never leave the database.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The leader can publish a draft; it becomes published, its first-published time is set, and its slug can no longer be changed.\n- [ ] The leader can unpublish a published post back to draft. The leader's own drafts publish directly.\n- [ ] Members cannot publish or unpublish: a direct POST returns 403.\n- [ ] `uv run cms publish` regenerates `site/` from scratch with: a home page showing one section per topic in fixed order with that topic's three newest published posts (title, nickname, date) and a *Ver todos* link, hiding topics with no published posts; all five topic pages, newest first, an empty one saying so; one page per published post with title, nickname, topic link, *Publicado el …* (Spanish date, Monterrey time UTC−6) and body.\n- [ ] Only published posts reach `site/`: a draft's title and body appear nowhere in the output, and a post unpublished since the last export disappears.\n- [ ] Markdown in the export is sanitized: a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute exports with neither.\n- [ ] Every `href` and `src` in `site/` is relative (no `href=\"/` or `src=\"/`), and a link to an accented slug is percent-encoded and resolves to a generated file.\n- [ ] Every public page has the striped navy-and-white header, a menu with *Inicio*, a row of topic links, and the disclaimer in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n- [ ] A post created through one app instance is still there through a new instance on the same database file.\n- [ ] The seed adds at least one published post per topic, including an obvious tiradera aimed at Tigres.\n- [ ] Manual: the exported site is deployed with `cms deploy` and loads at the GitHub Pages URL over HTTPS.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by: #3\n\n\n### T04: Members submit posts and the leader works a review queue\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nA member who has finished a draft submits it to the leader; until the leader acts, the member can withdraw it. The leader works through a review queue: publish, or send back to draft. The dashboard shows the counts, and the content list filters by status and topic.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A member submits their own draft; it becomes submitted. The member can withdraw their own submitted post back to draft.\n- [ ] A member cannot edit a submitted post directly (direct POST returns 403); they withdraw it first.\n- [ ] The leader can publish a submitted post or send it back to draft.\n- [ ] Members cannot send back or publish: direct POSTs return 403.\n- [ ] Submitted posts never appear in the export.\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts of drafts, submitted posts (labelled as waiting for review) and published posts.\n- [ ] The content list filters by status and by topic.\n- [ ] The seed adds one submitted post.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by: #4\n\n\n### T05: Members propose edits to published posts; the leader approves or sends them back\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nA member changes their own published post without taking it offline: the change waits as a pending edit while the published version stays public. The leader reviews the two side by side and approves or sends it back. Approved changes show *Actualizado el …* to readers.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A member saving changes to their own published post creates a pending edit (title, topic, body); the published version is unchanged in the admin console and in the export.\n- [ ] Saving again replaces the pending edit: a post has at most one.\n- [ ] A pending edit never changes the slug.\n- [ ] The leader sees the published version and the pending edit side by side. *Approve* replaces title, topic and body, removes the pending edit and marks the post as edited after publishing; the next export shows *Actualizado el …*.\n- [ ] *Send back* removes the pending edit and leaves the published version untouched.\n- [ ] Unpublishing a post with a pending edit is refused with a message.\n- [ ] The leader's direct edit of a published post saves immediately and marks it as edited after publishing.\n- [ ] Members cannot approve or send back, and cannot propose edits to another member's post: direct POSTs return 403.\n- [ ] Pending edits never appear in the export. Deleting a post deletes its pending edit.\n- [ ] The dashboard counts pending edits, and the content list can filter to posts with a pending edit.\n- [ ] The seed adds one published post with a pending edit.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by: #5\n\n\n### T08: The leader updates the site with one button, and the site gets its final look\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe leader puts every published change online with one *Actualizar el sitio* button, no terminal needed, and sees in plain Spanish what happened. The public site gets its finished look: a Cerro de la Silla banner on the home page and a stadium silhouette above the disclaimer, readable on a phone.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A leader-only *Actualizar el sitio* POST (with CSRF token) runs the export and then the upload, and reports each step (*\"Sitio generado ✓ · Subido a GitHub ✓\"*); if the upload fails it shows a plain Spanish error and the successful export still counts.\n- [ ] The time of the last successful export is recorded and shown on the dashboard.\n- [ ] Tests replace the upload with a fake; no test pushes to GitHub. Members get 403 (access-control test).\n- [ ] `uv run cms publish` and `uv run cms deploy` still work as before.\n- [ ] The home page has an original inline Cerro de la Silla banner and every public page has a generic stadium silhouette above the disclaimer; no image files, crest, logos or photos are used.\n- [ ] Manual: no horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page, the dashboard, the content list and the post editor.\n- [ ] The seed matches the spec's demo data list and runs clean from `.env.example` values.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by: #6, #7, #8","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"9704653d-dbdb-4140-9d84-4fbe8ffa2671","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:16:45.887Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"### T03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe leader publishes a post and, after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, readers see it on GitHub Pages: a home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, and a page per post with the author's nickname and a Spanish date, all inside the striped navy-and-white layout with the disclaimer. Monterrey) fan club. Not affiliated with the club. All names and content in this project are made up.\n\n## Who runs the site\nOne fan club leader. He got the job of being the admin for the whole thing. He knows the basics on a computer, nothing technical, so the admin side has to be simple.\n\n## Who writes\nThe members. Basically any fan who wants to share their opinion about the team: how a match went, what they think of the lineup, the coach, a signing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\nOther fans. They mostly want to express themselves and see what other people think. It's about opinions, not official news.\n\n## What's broken today\nRight now people post their opinions on X or Facebook. It works, but it's all mixed with everything else. I think a site just for this, just for Rayados fans, is better.\n\n## What would make it better\nOne place where the fan opinions live, organized, and easy to read.\n\n## What must never happen\nNo aggression toward other people. No threats against people or places. Trash talk toward other teams (tiraderas to Tigres, etc.) is fine, that's part of being a fan, but it can never cross into threats or attacking someone personally. That's why nothing should go public without the leader checking it first.\nnotes/client-brief.md:9:The members. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page**:\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":34,"oldLines":7,"newStart":34,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," ### Content"," ","-**Post**:","+**Post** (*Publicación*):"," A fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic."," _Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9c52a164-b5ad-4a14-a6b5-2b0ef2775556","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9bedde74-7160-4dff-9700-957083ce192b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Passwords come from\n# the environment there; in tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"lider@albiazul.example\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\",\n \"role\": \"editor\"},\n    \"editor2\": {\"email\": \"beto@albiazul.example\", \"password\": \"test-editor2-pw\",\n                \"nickname\": \"Furia del Cerro\", \"role\": \"editor\"},\n}\n\nCSRF_FIELD = re.compile(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"')\nPATH_PARAM = re.compile(r\"\\{[^}]+\\}\")\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef demo_users() -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    return DEMO_USERS\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef database_path(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:\n    path = tmp_path / \"cms.db\"\n    db.init(path)\n    conn = db.connect(path)\n    try:\n        for user in accounts.create_user(conn, email=user[\"email\"], password=user[\"password\"],\n                             role=user[\"role\"], nickname=user[\"nickname\"], active=False)\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    return user\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(database_path: Path) -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app(database_path))\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef csrf_token():\n return c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n                                      \"csrf_token\": token},\n                      follow_redirects=False)\n\n    return {"parentUuid":"5189f7f9-eed9-4f79-a519-b5496f59db50","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2cdac32f-54cc-46d2-94c0-21730bc710d0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the working-tree changes since f9475b7 (HEAD) for ticket #3 (T02), spec #1. But the screen field *Enlace* (slug) and *Vista previa* still have no CONTEXT.md entry.\n\n**S4 — Status is a bare string (Primitive Obsession; judgement).** `\"draft\"` appears in the `db.py` CHECK, in the `'draft'` literal in the INSERT, in the `STATUS_NAMES` keys, and in `policy.py` `post.status == \"draft\"`. The spec says tests go through HTTP. The code comment says this is temporary, so track replacing it in T03/T04.\n\n**S9 — Slug details (low).** The `slugify` docstring hard-codes \"80\" even though `SLUG_MAX` exists. `slugify(…) or SLUG_FALLBACK` is repeated in `_slug_for`; folding the fallback into `slugify` would remove the repeat.\n\n**Considered and dismissed:**\n- `author_id` and `author`: the glossary avoids \"author\" only as a role.\n- `may_change_post` reading the post's fields (Feature Envy): `policy.py`'s own docstring makes it \"the one place that says what a person may do\", and that documented rule wins.\n- `first_published_at` and `edited_at`: the spec's data model asks for them, so they aren't speculative.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>93544</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>11</tool_uses><duration_ms>134559</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"type":"queue-operation","operation":"enqueue","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:36:49.691Z","sessionId":"9bedde74-7160-4dff-9700-957083ce192b","content":"<task-notification>\n<task-id>a09f8079df44e7a32</task-id>\n<tool-use-id>toolu_0115nFmV9ZRrLDak2drsjHDm</tool-use-id>\n<output-file>/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91/tasks/a09f8079df44e7a32.output</output-file>\n<status>completed</status>\n<summary>Agent \"Spec review of T02 diff\" finished</summary>\n<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no missing acceptance criteria and no real scope creep: all nine ACs on #3 are implemented, the 90 tests pass, and each test name says which criterion it covers. What's left is one structural gap and five small ones.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n- **P1, lifecycle not in Content.** Spec: *\"Content. … the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\"* `content.save_post` and `content.delete_post` accept any post in any status. The only gate is `policy.may_change_post`, attached as a route dependency. That one check covers three different rows of the table (Save, Edit directly, Delete). T05's \"Propose edit\" (a member saving their own published post) will have to split it. This is the most important finding.\n- **P2, leader editing is only half tested.** AC: *\"The leader can edit any post.\"* `test_leader_edits_any_members_post` only covers a member's draft. No test has the leader save a submitted or published post.\n- **P3, an error with no Spanish message.** Spec: *\"Unknown ids get 404.\"* AC: *\"Every save, delete and error shows a message.\"* I checked: `GET /admin/posts/abc` returns 422 with a raw English JSON body, not the Spanish page.\n- **P4, create skips Policy.** Spec: *\"Policy … Every write route asks it.\"* `POST /admin/posts/new` never asks Policy. The behaviour is correct today (any signed-in user may create), but it breaks that rule.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n\nNone worth acting on. The `\"publicación\"` fallback slug, Monterrey time in the admin, and the 404 page are needed or follow from the spec. Refusing a manual slug that isn't already in final form (uppercase is refused, not lowercased) is a fair reading of *\"an invalid manual slug is refused with a message.\"*\n\n**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n\n- **P5, a taken manual slug is changed silently.** Spec: *\"A manually entered slug follows the same rules.\"* So `-2` is a defensible choice. But I checked: typing `uno` when it's taken saves as `uno-2`, and the person only sees \"Borrador guardado.\", with nothing saying their link was changed. That clashes with *\"Every save … shows a message.\"* No test covers this decision.\n- **P6, wording on the leader's editor.** For a submitted or published post the leader still sees **\"Guardar borrador\"**, and the help text says *\"Puedes cambiarlo hasta que la publicación se publique.\"* That sentence shows the trouble with the glossary choice: *Publicación* (Post) and *Publicada* (Published) share a root, and \"publicación\" also means \"the act of publishing.\" Add an _Avoid_ note in `CONTEXT.md`, or reword the help text.\n\n**The implementer's decisions**\n\n- Leaving the slug lock to T03 is right (T03 AC1). Not setting `edited_at` when the leader edits a published post belongs to T05 (its AC7). Leaving the filters to T04 is also right.\n- Setting the status in storage to test \"own drafts only\" is acceptable and matches T01. The test's comment explains it.\n- The Spanish 404 page meets the spec.\n- The CSRF replay and access-matrix tests from T01 find the new routes automatically, so the preview POSTs are covered twice.\n- Seed (AC9) is covered by `test_seed_adds_one_draft_written_by_a_member`.\n\nI didn't edit any files. For the probes I briefly copied a test file into `tests/` and deleted it right away; `git status` shows nothing left behind.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>87526</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>12</tool_uses><duration_ms>128433</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"d3b33d18-0d31-410e-b73b-b901ece47df0","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1c1d766f-239f-4ee7-a161-7c86a8ce1e75","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/receiving-code-review\n\n# Code Review Reception\n\n## Overview\n\nCode review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.\n\n**Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.\n\n## The Response Pattern\n\n```\nWHEN receiving code review feedback:\n\n1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting\n2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)\n3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality\n4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?\n5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback\n6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each\n```\n\n## Forbidden Responses\n\n**NEVER:**\n- \"You're absolutely right!\" (explicit instruction-file violation)\n- \"Great point!\" / \"Excellent feedback!\" (performative)\n- \"Let me implement that now\" (before verification)\n\n**INSTEAD:**\n- Restate the technical requirement\n- Ask clarifying questions\n- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong\n- Just start working (actions > words)\n\n## Handling Unclear Feedback\n\n```\nIF any item is unclear:\n  STOP - do not implement anything yet\n  ASK for clarification on unclear items\n\nWHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.\n```\n\n**Example:**\n```\nyour human partner: \"Fix 1-6\"\nYou understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.\n\n❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later\n✅ RIGHT: \"I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding.\"\n```\n\n## Source-Specific Handling\n\n### From your human partner\n- **Trusted** - implement after understanding\n- **Still ask** if scope unclear\n- **No performative agreement**\n- **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment\n\n### From External Reviewers\n```\nBEFORE implementing:\n  1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?\n  2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?\n  3. Check: Reason for current implementation?\n  4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?\n  5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?\n\nIF suggestion seems wrong:\n  Push back with technical reasoning\n\nIF can't easily verify:\n  Say so: \"I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?\"\n\nIF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions:\n  Stop and discuss with your human partner first\n```\n\n**your human partner's rule:** \"External feedback - be skeptical, but check carefully\"\n\n## YAGNI Check for \"Professional\" Features\n\n```\nIF reviewer suggests \"implementing properly\":\n  grep codebase for actual usage\n\n  IF unused: \"This endpoint isn't called. Remove it (YAGNI)?\"\n  IF used: Then implement properly\n```\n\n**your human partner's rule:** \"You and reviewer both report to me. If we don't need this feature, don't add it.\"\n\n## Implementation Order\n\n```\nFOR multi-item feedback:\n  1. Clarify anything unclear FIRST\n  2. Then implement in this order:\n     - Blocking issues (breaks, security)\n     - Simple fixes (typos, imports)\n     - Complex fixes (refactoring, logic)\n  3. Test each fix individually\n  4. Verify no regressions\n```\n\n## When To Push Back\n\nPush back when:\n- Suggestion breaks existing functionality\n- Reviewer lacks full context\n- Violates YAGNI (unused feature)\n- Technically incorrect for this stack\n- Legacy/compatibility reasons exist\n- Conflicts with your human partner's architectural decisions\n\n**How to push back:**\n- Use technical reasoning, not defensiveness\n- Ask specific questions\n- Reference working tests/code\n- Involve your human partner if architectural\n\n**If you're uncomfortable pushing back out loud:** Name that tension, then tell your partner about the issue you've seen. They'll appreciate your honesty.\n\n## Acknowledging Correct Feedback\n\nWhen feedback IS correct:\n```\n✅ \"Fixed. [Brief description of what changed]\"\n✅ \"Good catch - [specific issue]. Fixed in [location].\"\n✅ [Just fix it and show in the code]\n\n❌ \"You're absolutely right!\"\n❌ \"Great point!\"\n❌ \"Thanks for catching that!\"\n❌ \"Thanks for [anything]\"\n❌ ANY gratitude expression\n```\n\n**Why no thanks:** Actions speak. Just fix it. The code itself shows you heard the feedback.\n\n**If you catch yourself about to write \"Thanks\":** DELETE IT. State the fix instead.\n\n## Gracefully Correcting Your Pushback\n\nIf you pushed back and were wrong:\n```\n✅ \"You were right - I checked [X] and it does [Y]. Implementing now.\"\n✅ \"Verified this and you're correct. My initial understanding was wrong because [reason]. Fixing.\"\n\n❌ Long apology\n❌ Defending why you pushed back\n❌ Over-explaining\n```\n\nState the correction factually and move on.\n\n## Common Mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n|---------|-----|\n| Performative agreement | State requirement or just act |\n| Blind implementation | Verify against codebase first |\n| Batch without testing | One at a time, test each |\n| Assuming reviewer is right | Check if breaks things |\n| Avoiding pushback | Technical correctness > comfort |\n| Partial implementation | Clarify all items first |\n| Can't verify, proceed anyway | State limitation, ask for direction |\n\n## Real Examples\n\n**Performative Agreement (Bad):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Remove legacy code\"\n❌ \"You're absolutely right! Let me remove that...\"\n```\n\n**Technical Verification (Good):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Remove legacy code\"\n✅ \"Checking... build target is 10.15+, this API needs 13+. Need legacy for backward compat. Current impl has wrong bundle ID - fix it or drop pre-13 support?\"\n```\n\n**YAGNI (Good):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Implement proper metrics tracking with database, date filters, CSV export\"\n✅ \"Grepped codebase - nothing calls this endpoint. Remove it (YAGNI)? Or is there usage I'm missing?\"\n```\n\n**Unclear Item (Good):**\n```\nyour human partner: \"Fix items 1-6\"\nYou understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.\n✅ \"Understand 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before implementing.\"\n```\n\n## GitHub Thread Replies\n\nWhen replying to inline review comments on GitHub, reply in the comment thread (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies`), not as a top-level PR comment.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"051458c3-b693-4cd0-90ae-402479af38f7","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:37:23.014Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_018wksEYz28tynWQ47wTiThe","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9bedde74-7160-4dff-9700-957083ce192b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no missing acceptance criteria and no real scope creep: all nine ACs on #3 are implemented, the 90 tests pass, and each test name says which criterion it covers. What's left is one structural gap and five small ones.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n- **P1, lifecycle not in Content.** Spec: *\"Content. … the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\"* `content.save_post` and `content.delete_post` accept any post in any status. The only gate is `policy.may_change_post`, attached as a route dependency. That one check covers three different rows of the table (Save, Edit directly, Delete). T05's \"Propose edit\" (a member saving their own published post) will have to split it. This is the most important finding.\n- **P2, leader editing is only half tested.** AC: *\"The leader can edit any post.\"* `test_leader_edits_any_members_post` only covers a member's draft. No test has the leader save a submitted or published post.\n- **P3, an error with no Spanish message.** Spec: *\"Unknown ids get 404.\"* AC: *\"Every save, delete and error shows a message.\"* I checked: `GET /admin/posts/abc` returns 422 with a raw English JSON body, not the Spanish page.\n- **P4, create skips Policy.** Spec: *\"Policy … Every write route asks it.\"* `POST /admin/posts/new` never asks Policy. The behaviour is correct today (any signed-in user may create), but it breaks that rule.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n\nNone worth acting on. The `\"publicación\"` fallback slug, Monterrey time in the admin, and the 404 page are needed or follow from the spec. Refusing a manual slug that isn't already in final form (uppercase is refused, not lowercased) is a fair reading of *\"an invalid manual slug is refused with a message.\"*\n\n**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n\n- **P5, a taken manual slug is changed silently.** Spec: *\"A manually entered slug follows the same rules.\"* So `-2` is a defensible choice. But I checked: typing `uno` when it's taken saves as `uno-2`, and the person only sees \"Borrador guardado.\", with nothing saying their link was changed. That clashes with *\"Every save … shows a message.\"* No test covers this decision.\n- **P6, wording on the leader's editor.** For a submitted or published post the leader still sees **\"Guardar borrador\"**, and the help text says *\"Puedes cambiarlo hasta que la publicación se publique.\"* That sentence shows the trouble with the glossary choice: *Publicación* (Post) and *Publicada* (Published) share a root, and \"publicación\" also means \"the act of publishing.\" Add an _Avoid_ note in `CONTEXT.md`, or reword the help text.\n\n**The implementer's decisions**\n\n- Leaving the slug lock to T03 is right (T03 AC1). Not setting `edited_at` when the leader edits a published post belongs to T05 (its AC7). Leaving the filters to T04 is also right.\n- Setting the status in storage to test \"own drafts only\" is acceptable and matches T01. The test's comment explains it.\n- The Spanish 404 page meets the spec.\n- The CSRF replay and access-matrix tests from T01 find the new routes automatically, so the preview POSTs are covered twice.\n- Seed (AC9) is covered by `test_seed_adds_one_draft_written_by_a_member`.\n\nI didn't edit any files. For the probes I briefly copied a test file into `tests/` and deleted it right away; `git status` shows nothing left behind.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>87526</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>12</tool_uses><duration_ms>128433</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>","reason":"absorbed_mid_turn","commandUuid":"2ee807ec-adb9-4e21-a58d-ca9c5149fa8c","deliveryId":"7deefdb7-b439-4b50-a7d1-b1d5d3817dfd"}

Puedes cambiarlo hasta que la publicación se publique.</p>\n20\t    <label for=\"topic\">Tema</label>\n21\t    <select id=\"topic\" name=\"topic\" required>\n22\t      <option value=\"\">Elige un tema</option>\n23\t      {% for key, name in topics.items() %}\n24\t      <option value=\"{{ key }}\"{% if form.topic == key %} selected{% endif %}>{{ name }}</option>\n25\t      {% endfor %}\n26\t    </select>\n27\t    <label for=\"body\">Texto (Markdown)</label>\n28\t    <textarea id=\"body\" name=\"body\" rows=\"14\">{{ form.body }}</textarea>\n29\t    <div class=\"actions\">\n30\t      <button class=\"primary\" type=\"submit\">Guardar borrador</button>\n31\t      <button type=\"submit\" formaction=\"{{ url_for('preview_post', post_id=post.id) if post else url_for('preview_new_post') }}\">Vista previa</button>\n32\t      {% if post %}<a class=\"danger\" href=\"{{ url_for('confirm_delete_post', post_id=post.id) }}\">Borrar</a>{% endif %}\n33\t    </div>\n34\t  </form>\n35\t  {% if preview_html is defined %}\n36\t  <section class=\"preview\" aria-label=\"Vista previa\">\n37\t    <h2>Vista previa</h2>\n38\t    <p class=\"help\">Así lo verán los lectores. Todavía no se ha guardado.</p>\n39\t    <div class=\"preview-body\">{{ preview_html | safe }}</div>\n40\t  </section>\n41\t  {% endif %}\n42\t{% endblock %}\n43\t"}]},"uuid":"2bf3d7e6-d1a0-41a8-9a91-2d7d132f0525","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:39:54.772Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/templates/admin/post_form.html","content":"{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block title %}{{ post.title if post else \"Nueva publicación\" }}{% endblock %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>{{ post.title if post else \"Nueva publicación\" }}</h1>\n  {% if post %}\n  <p class=\"meta\">\n    {{ post.status_name }} · de {{ post.author_nickname or \"—\" }} ·\n    Creada: {{ post.created_at | monterrey_time }} ·\n    Última actualización: {{ post.updated_at | monterrey_time }}\n  </p>\n  {% endif %}\n  {% if error %}<p class=\"error\" role=\"alert\">{{ error }}</p>{% endif %}\n  <form method=\"post\" action=\"{{ url_for('save_post', post_id=post.id) if post else url_for('create_post') }}\">\n    <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token(request) }}\">\n    <label for=\"title\">Título</label>\n    <input id=\"title\" name=\"title\" type=\"text\" value=\"{{ form.title }}\" required>\n    <label for=\"slug\">Enlace</label>\n    <input id=\"slug\" name=\"slug\" type=\"text\" value=\"{{ form.slug }}\" placeholder=\"Se crea a partir del título\" aria-describedby=\"slug-help\">\n    <p id=\"slug-help\" class=\"help\">Solo letras minúsculas, números y guiones. Puedes cambiarlo hasta que la publicación se publique.</p>\n    <label for=\"topic\">Tema</label>\n    <select id=\"topic\" name=\"topic\" required>\n      <option value=\"\">Elige un tema</option>\n      {% for key, name in topics.items() %}\n      <option value=\"{{ key }}\"{% if form.topic == key %} selected{% endif %}>{{ name }}</option>\n      {% endfor %}\n    </select>\n    <label for=\"body\">Texto (Markdown)</label>\n    <textarea id=\"body\" name=\"body\" rows=\"14\">{{ form.body }}</textarea>\n    <div class=\"actions\">\n      <button class=\"primary\" type=\"submit\">Guardar borrador</button>\n      <button type=\"submit\" formaction=\"{{ url_for('preview_post', post_id=post.id) if post else url_for('preview_new_post') }}\">Vista previa</button>\n      {% if post %}<a class=\"danger\" href=\"{{ url_for('confirm_delete_post', post_id=post.id) }}\">Borrar</a>{% endif %}\n    </div>\n  </form>\n  {% if preview_html is defined %}\n  <section class=\"preview\" aria-label=\"Vista previa\">\n    <h2>Vista previa</h2>\n    <p class=\"help\">Así lo verán los lectores. Todavía no se ha guardado.</p>\n    <div class=\"preview-body\">{{ preview_html | safe }}</div>\n  </section>\n  {% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n","numLines":43,"startLine":1,"totalLines":43}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"87bc09ab-0992-485d-ba8a-ae03e09d3908","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9bedde74-7160-4dff-9700-957083ce192b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

In Spanish, *publicación* is always the thing, never the act: for the act say *publicar*.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry; \"la publicación de …\" to mean publishing\n\n**Slug** (*Enlace*):\nThe end of a post's web address, made from its title (`crónica-del-clásico-regio`). It can be changed until the post is first published, then never, so links shared on X or Facebook keep working.\n_Avoid_: URL, permalink, path\n\n**Preview** (*Vista previa*):\nA post's Markdown shown exactly as readers will see it, sanitized, without saving anything.\n_Avoid_: Draft view, render","originalFile":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post** (*Publicación*):\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page**:\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft** (*Borrador*):\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted** (*Enviada*):\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published** (*Publicada*):\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":35,"oldLines":9,"newStart":35,"newLines":17,"lines":[" ### Content"," "," **Post** (*Publicación*):","-A fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.","-_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry","+A fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.
